host_placement_without_cache.placement: --cpu-moe retains all expert weights in host memory; --n-cpu-moe N does so for the first N layers. Other offloaded layers/tensors still use Vulkan.
host_placement_without_cache.execution: Pinned Vulkan offload_op accepts host operations when op batch size >=32 (default GGML_OP_OFFLOAD_MIN_BATCH; no GGML environment overrides observed). Thus ordinary host placement is not equivalent to all-CPU execution: single-token/small decode expert work remains CPU-scheduled, while sufficiently large prefill operations can be transferred/offloaded to Vulkan.
host_placement_without_cache.evidence_limit: Source-backed scheduling interpretation plus allocation logs and measured CPU cost, not a per-kernel profiler trace. No claim that every operation or every prefill node uses the same device.

dynamic_expert_cache.placement: Expert backing weights remain host-resident; GPU banks contain an LRU subset. Missing selected experts are uploaded; hits reuse bank slots. Cache weights are marked device weights so operations reading them execute on that device.
dynamic_expert_cache.limits: get_slot_map bypasses n_tokens==0, n_tokens>32, or an insufficient selected-expert slot budget. Tensor-parallel split mode is explicitly rejected by the pinned constructor.
dynamic_expert_cache.prefill_nuance: The >32 bypass is for slot-map/cache-routing, NOT all cache use. copy_experts can copy already-cached experts into large-batch staging without disturbing the decode LRU. Destructor counters distinguish ubatch<=8, ubatch>8 (eligible small batches), and large-batch copies.

runtime_execution_proof.source_record: results/new-cpu-moe-cache1024.json placement_cache_log and external per-run server.log

allocation_limit.signature: Requested buffer size exceeds device buffer size limit: ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory
allocation_limit.interpretation: Pinned ggml-vulkan-buffers.cpp explicitly rejects size>device.max_buffer_size before allocation. The device maximum comes from maintenance4 maxBufferSize, unless overridden. No override was observed. This failure is a bank-size/backend/device-limit result, not evidence that total 24-GiB VRAM was exhausted. No forced unsupported buffer-size override or upstream modification was attempted.
